Reflections on a COIL Project: Insights and Recommendations for Future Collaboration in the Metaverse
abstract: The metaverse has emerged as an increasingly popular platform for collaborative teaching and learning. This study presents reflections from three instructors who have used a metaverse platform (FrameVR. io), alongside other virtual modalities, in a Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL) project. The instructors reflected on their students’ virtual exchanges and discussions within these platforms, as well as their insights into how such environments can support future international and intercultural interaction. The findings suggest that, when purposefully integrated into COIL, the metaverse can enrich both intercultural learning and teacher development. This potential, however, depends on thoughtful design, ongoing reflection, and pedagogical flexibility. This study, therefore, encourages educators to view the metaverse not as a novelty but as an evolving ecosystem for collaborative learning and intercultural growth.

title: Modeling Active Collaborative Learning in Online Education: Effects of Social Presence, Tutor Interaction, and Learner Attitude
abstract: This study investigates how peer interaction, tutor interaction, and social presence shape active collaborative learning in fully online higher education, specifying elearning attitude as a central mediator. Survey data from 357 students enrolled in distance courses at a Vietnamese open university were analyzed using variance-based structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM, SmartPLS 4). Tutor interaction and social presence exhibited significant direct effects on collaborative learning, whereas peer interaction influenced collaborative learning indirectly through elearning attitude. The direct path from peer interaction to collaborative learning was nonsignificant, which is consistent with the mediating role of elearning attitude. Out-of-sample predictive assessment via PLS-Predict and the Cross-Validated Predictive Ability Test (CVPAT) showed that, on average, the PLS-SEM model achieved lower prediction loss than a linear benchmark, while acknowledging isolated indicators for which the benchmark performed comparably or better. title: Usage Pattern of Open Educational Resources (OER) Among University Students: An Exploratory Study
abstract: This study investigates Kurukshetra University students’ awareness, usage, preferences, and perceptions of Open Educational Resources (OER) and emphasizes the role of each in enhancing education. Using stratified random sampling, a descriptive survey methodology was employed to select 150 students from engineering, sciences, and management faculties. With a response rate of 94.7%, data from 142 valid questionnaires were analyzed using percentages, means, standard deviations, and chi-square tests at a 0.05 significance level. Findings are presented in descriptive tables for clarity. The study shows that students are generally aware of and actively engage with OER. Key drivers of OER adoption include cost-effectiveness, improved accessibility, updated information, and sustainability. Open textbooks are the most preferred resource, followed by video lectures, open-access journals, and social media platforms. Students also use digital tools to create, modify, and share OER while adhering to copyright and licensing guidelines. title: Enhancing Creative Problem-Solving Skills Through Project-Based Blended Learning in Higher Education
abstract: The study explores the impact of the Project Based Blended Learning (PBBL) model on students’ Creative Problem-Solving (CPS) skills. Despite the use of Project-Based Learning in teaching, deficiencies in student creativity persist, highlighting the need for innovative pedagogical approaches. Creativity in problem-solving is crucial in the Industrial Revolution 4.0 era, particularly in higher education. Preliminary investigations in early 2024 revealed that students struggle with creativity in project-based assignments. This quasi-experimental study used a posttest-only control group design involving fifth-semester undergraduate students enrolled in the 2024/2025 academic year. Data were collected through CPS tests, student response questionnaires, and interviews. The experimental group received Project Based Blended Learning treatment, while the control group engaged with Project Based Learning. A t-test and coded responses to an interview were used to analyze the posttest results. Findings indicate that Project Based Blended Learning significantly enhanced CPS skills compared to Project Based Learning. title: Virtual Reality Tours: Exploring Student Perspective-Taking in a 360-Degree Courtroom Tour
abstract: Scholarship recognizes that virtual reality (VR) simulations offer students authentic learning opportunities that support perspective-taking, but the value of VR tours for perspectival thinking is underexplored. Drawing on inductive qualitative thematic analysis, this study investigates how students alternatively reflect on and embody perspectives in a 360-degree VR courtroom tour. Findings indicate that students adopted enactive or observational perspectives to cultivate a sense of presence and support their understanding of courtroom design, spatial layout, and courtroom roles and practices. These findings underscore the importance of considering student knowledge and prior experience in VR learning design.

title: Assessing LMS Quality and Satisfaction for Students With Disabilities in Higher Education
abstract: This study examines the use of elearning among students with disabilities in higher education by focusing on their satisfaction with Learning Management Systems (LMSs). Using a quantitative survey design, questionnaires were distributed to 88 students with disabilities who had used an LMS for more than two semesters. Data were collected based on the DeLone and McLean Information Systems success model, which measures four quality dimensions of system quality, information quality, service quality, and user satisfaction. The following four hypotheses were proposed: (1) System quality affects user satisfaction, (2) Information quality affects user satisfaction, (3) Service quality affects user satisfaction, and (4) User satisfaction affects individual impact. The data were analyzed using SEM-PLS with SmartPLS, and all four hypotheses were supported. The results show that students with disabilities can effectively adapt to LMS-based learning and perceive the system as supportive of their learning needs.

title: Retaining First-Year Nontraditional Online Higher Education Students: A Qualitative Exploratory Study
abstract: Research suggests that complex factors contribute to first-year student retention and successful degree completion in online higher educational institutions. The availability of support may develop students’ self-confidence, strengthen self-efficacy, promote self-directed learning, and improve performance and retention. This qualitative, exploratory case study explores how online higher education institutions may improve the retention of nontraditional online students. Since Tinto and Cullen’s (1973) model addressed the experiences of on-campus students, its applicability to the online environment is limited. The results have universality for the global community of online higher education institutions and may contribute to a comprehensive attrition model designed specifically for online learning.

title: Artificial Intelligence in the Classroom: Tools for Personalizing the Educational Experience in Higher Education
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming higher education, establishing itself as a catalyst for change that enables the personalization of the educational experience. In contrast to traditional, one-size-fits-all models, AI tailors learning to the individual needs, paces, and styles of students through tools such as intelligent tutoring systems and adaptive platforms. This article aims to analyze the impact of AI on the personalization of learning in higher education by identifying the most widely used tools and their benefits, limitations, and implementation challenges. The research adopts a hermeneutic-documentary approach, based on the systematic review and critical interpretation of 30 academic articles selected from an initial corpus of 584 articles published between 2019 and 2024. A wide range of AI tools (e.g., adaptive systems, chatbots, automated assessment) were identified that enhance personalization, provide immediate feedback, and improve accessibility and teaching efficiency. title: Can a Bot Heal Writing Anxiety? A Study on ChatGPT, Teacher Feedback, and Student Enjoyment
abstract: Writing anxiety and enjoyment are key affective factors influencing EFL students’ writing development. This study adopted a mixed-methods approach to examine the emotional impact of ChatGPT-generated feedback and online teacher feedback on Indonesian EFL students’ writing anxiety and enjoyment. Fifty undergraduate students were divided into two groups: 26 received automated feedback from ChatGPT, while 24 received teacher feedback via Padlet. Quantitative data were gathered using preand posttests based on the English Writing Anxiety Scale (EWAS) and the English Writing Enjoyment Scale (EWES), along with closed-ended perception questionnaires. Qualitative data were collected through open-ended questionnaire responses to explore students’ perceived effectiveness and affective experiences with the feedback. Quantitative findings showed that both groups experienced nonsignificant reductions in writing anxiety, while only the teacher feedback group reported a significant increase in writing enjoyment. title: Beyond the Screen: The Value of On-Campus Intensives in Virtual Nursing Education
abstract: The Master of Science in Nursing, Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP) Online program at a small private institution in the northeastern United States requires an on-campus intensive (OCI) residency that focuses on achieving learning objectives such as clinical skill development and provider-level patient management. MSN FNP Online students were required to attend a one-day, on-ground residency event in the first semester and final semester of each student’s matriculation plan. During the 8-hour OCI residency day, a sample of 30 FNP students answered a survey to assess their perceptions of meeting benchmark objectives, evaluate the presenters, and provide their overall satisfaction with the event. The feedback provided suggests that the OCI experiences may have enhanced the learning and engagement of students and promoted the connections made among students and faculty. This outcome highlights the value of incorporating in-person components into FNP programs conducted primarily online.

title: A Competency-Based Smart Classroom Framework for Language Instruction in Higher Education
abstract: The goal of this study was to create a holistic competence profile for language-teaching lecturers at institutions of higher education that incorporates pedagogical, digital, and institutional dimensions. The methodology adopted in this study was an exploratory design using a mixed-methods strategy that included 120 lecturers in the three main regions of Java. The findings demonstrate that the lecturers had a mediocre to good knowledge of the core concepts of the smart classroom and were comparatively well-prepared for the technology. However, the implementation of active learning strategies remains uneven and institutional support is not yet fully maximized. The lecturers’ reflections indicated a high motivation for them to innovate, but they still lacked training and sufficient technical support. The results informed the generation of a Competency-Based Smart Classroom Framework that may function as a foundation of theoretical and practical insights for implementing technology-based learning effectively and sustainably at the tertiary level. The framework has the potential to guide training, policy, and classroom practice at the university level.

title: Contributions, Weaknesses, Challenges, and Impediments of Virtual Reality: A Systematic Literature Review in Open and Distance Learning
abstract: The use of Virtual Reality continues to increase and has become a prominent feature in Open and Distance Learning. However, there are gaps in the literature contains gaps and uncertainties regarding its impact on learning access and equity. This study systematic literature review aims to explore VR’s contributions, weaknesses, challenges, and impediments in enhancing learning access and equity in distance learning. We found 10,170 academic works on this topic from last decade sourced from ScienceDirect, Scholar, and OpenAlex. Our initial search was conducted to find studies related to the research topic and then the results were screened until we finalized and 27 published academic works that we analyzed using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) method. We coded the results and came up with four categories for VR analysis: its contributions, weaknesses, challenges, and impediments. The findings indicate that the integration of VR into higher education should take into account many factors related to the categories to maximize its benefits. title: AI-Powered Personalized Learning: Enhancing Student Academic Achievement and Motivation
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) applications have driven education toward more adaptive and personalized learning experiences and environments. By offering educators tools to customize learning paths, adapt resources to students’ needs, and provide tailored feedback, AI applications are able to boost student academic achievement and motivation. This study seeks to assess the impact of an AI-enhanced learning approach on students’ academic achievement and motivation. We employed a quasi-experimental method for this study with a total of 54 sixth-grade pupils at a private bilingual school in Barka, Oman split into an experimental group and a control group. The experimental group was taught using AI applications and the control group was taught using the Moodle learning management system. title: Enhancing Digital Learning Through Spatial Contiguity: A Meta-Analysis Study
abstract: This meta-analysis study investigates how the spatial contiguity principle (the proximity of related text and visuals within the same spatial setting) influences learning outcomes in digital learning environments. I systematically reviewed and meta-analyzed 28 empirical studies published 1991–2025, involving 4,720 learners in the K–12, higher education, and corporate training settings, to estimate the overall effect of spatial contiguity and examine moderators such as instruction type and learner expertise. The findings revealed a moderate to strong overall effect of spatial contiguity on retention and comprehension, with Hedges’ g = 0.73. The findings also revealed that animated instruction modes had the largest effect size (Hedges’ g = 0.78). Moreover, novice learners benefited more from spatially contiguous designs (Hedges’ g = 0.75) than experienced learners. This highlights how important it is to tailor instructional content to fit the expertise levels of learners. The present study emphasizes the important role played by spatial contiguity in reducing extraneous cognitive load during learning. title: Every Student Succeeds: Amplifying Voices in Times of Crisis
abstract: This study incorporated a descriptive quantitative research design to examine students’ and parents’ experiences with the sudden transition to online learning during the COVID-19 pandemic. The research aims to provide insights into how these experiences shaped modern educational practices and guide teacher preparation programs in supporting students’ ability to navigate online and hybrid spaces. Findings highlight students’ frustrations with unexpected changes, their desire for more social interaction, and their ability to differentiate effective from ineffective online instructional strategies. Additionally, the study reveals how remote learning fostered growth in soft skills, including executive function and adaptability. While social-emotional learning (SEL) played a role in student engagement and community building, it was one of several factors shaping the online learning experience. The study’s recommendations emphasize the importance of integrating effective pedagogy into online instruction to improve student experiences, strengthen engagement, and support resilience in digital learning environments.
